definition: the ways something worth doing leaves my life with no decision to stop it

settled:
Fast early progress, then a plateau, then a defensive quit. I am a serial quitter that way. The quit is a flinch at the moment progress stalls rather than a verdict on the thing, and the tell is that I come back to what is genuinely valuable once the shock fades.

A break taken for a real reason, an injury say, has no return cue built into it, so it never expires. Weeks later a temporary stop and a permanent one look the same. Anything stopped for a passing reason needs a cue outside me to restart it.

Starting a lapsed thing again costs more than keeping it going, so re-entry waits on a higher safety level than upkeep ever needed. For about six weeks below that level a restart of the game was simply not an option. As my safety settles at four to five the re-entry comes back within reach. Upkeep would have been affordable the whole time.

When something valuable lapses the move is to take the stack apart rather than to summon willpower again.

title: How A Good Thing Quietly Stops
